stem: The division based on the social expectations from men and women is known as the:
solution: Gender division is a form of hierarchical social division seen everywhere, based on social expectations and stereotypes rather than biology alone.

stem: The belief that men and women have different roles — women managing the home and men working outside — is based on:
options: The gendered division of labour and social conditioning
solution: The gender division tends to be understood as natural and unchangeable, but it is based on social expectations and stereotypes — the gendered division of labour, in which women are expected to do domestic work.

stem: The word 'feminist' refers to:
options: A person who believes in equal rights and opportunities for women and men
solution: A feminist is a woman or man who believes in equal rights and opportunities for women and men.

stem: The political expression of the gender division and political mobilisation on this question helped to improve women's role in public life. These movements are called:
solution: The political expression of gender divisions and political mobilisation on this question helped improve women's role in public life; radical women's movements aimed at equality are called feminist movements.

stem: According to the Census, the literacy rate among women in India is significantly:
solution: The literacy rate among women is only 54 per cent compared with 76 per cent among men — a wide gender gap in education.

stem: The proportion of women in the highly paid and valued jobs is still very small because:
options: On average, girls are given less education and equal work is often paid less; a smaller proportion of girls go for higher studies
There are laws against women working
solution: A smaller proportion of girls go for higher studies; wherever women do wage work, they are often paid less than men even for the same work, so the proportion of women in highly paid jobs remains small.

stem: The Equal Remuneration Act of 1976 provides that:
options: Women should not work at night
Equal wages should be paid to equal work regardless of sex
solution: The Equal Remuneration Act, 1976, provides that equal wages should be paid to equal work; yet in almost all areas of work, from sports to cinema and factories to fields, women are paid less than men.

stem: The falling sex ratio (child sex ratio) in some parts of India is largely due to:
options: Sex-selective abortion and preference for a male child
solution: In many parts of India, parents prefer sons and want daughters to be born only when there is already a son; this preference and female foeticide (sex-selective abortion) have led to a decline in the child sex ratio.

stem: The number of girl children per thousand boys, i.e., the child sex ratio, in India has been:
solution: The child sex ratio (number of girl children per thousand boys) has been declining and is well below the natural level, dropping to about 919 in the 2011 Census.

stem: One important measure to increase women's participation in political decision-making has been:
options: Reservation of one-third seats in local government bodies (panchayats and municipalities)
Increasing the voting age for women
solution: One-third of seats in local government bodies — panchayats and municipalities — are now reserved for women; there are more than 10 lakh elected women representatives in rural and urban local bodies.

stem: In the Indian legislatures (Lok Sabha), the proportion of women members has:
options: Never reached even 15% until recently — among the lowest in the world
Been decided by reservation from the start
solution: The percentage of elected women members in the Lok Sabha has for long remained low, touching about 14 per cent of its total strength for the first time in 2019 — among the lowest in the world.

stem: Women's organisations and activists have been demanding a similar reservation of at least one-third seats in:
options: The Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies
solution: Women's organisations and activists have been demanding a similar reservation of at least one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies; a bill to this effect has been pending before the Parliament.

stem: In India, communalism was and continues to be one of the major challenges to democracy. Communalism refers to a situation when:
options: Religion is seen as the basis of the nation and one religion's followers are pitted against another's
solution: Communalism involves the belief that people belonging to the same religion share common interests and can form one community; in its extreme form it leads to the belief that people of different religions cannot live as equal citizens.

stem: The most common expression of communalism is in everyday beliefs which involve:
options: Religious prejudices, stereotypes of religious communities and belief in the superiority of one's religion
solution: The most common expression of communalism is in everyday beliefs — religious prejudices, stereotypes of religious communities, and belief in the superiority of one's religion over other religions.

stem: When beliefs of one religion are presented as superior to those of other religions and the demands of one religious group are formed in opposition to another, it takes the form of:
solution: Communalism in politics involves the political dominance of one religious group and its interests being pitted against those of another — communal politics.

stem: The most extreme and ugly form that communalism can take is:
solution: Communalism can take its most ugly form of communal violence, riots and massacre; India and Pakistan suffered some of the worst communal riots at the time of Partition.

stem: A secular state is one which:
options: Does not have an official religion and treats all religions equally, giving freedom to practise any or none
solution: A secular state is one that does not establish any one religion as official; the Indian Constitution provides that there is no official religion, freedom to profess any religion, and that the state shall not discriminate on grounds of religion.

stem: Which of the following is NOT a provision of the Indian Constitution regarding secularism?
options: There is no official religion for the Indian state
The Constitution provides freedom to profess, practise and propagate any religion
The Constitution establishes Hinduism as the state religion
The Constitution allows the state to intervene in religious matters to ensure equality
solution: The Indian Constitution does not establish any state religion; it gives freedom to all to practise, profess and propagate any religion or none, and prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion.

stem: The Indian Constitution allows the state to intervene in the affairs of religion in order to:
options: Ensure equality within religious communities, e.g., banning untouchability
solution: The Constitution allows the state to intervene in matters of religion to ensure equality within religious communities — for example, it bans untouchability, which was practised in the name of religion.

stem: Caste division is special to which country?
solution: Caste division is special to India; hereditary occupational division sanctioned by rituals gave rise to the caste system.

stem: The caste system is based on:
options: Exclusion of and discrimination against 'outcaste' groups and hereditary occupational division sanctioned by rituals
solution: Members of the same caste group were supposed to form a social community that practised the same or similar occupation, married within the caste group, and did not eat with members of other caste groups — based on exclusion and hereditary occupation sanctioned by rituals.

stem: Political leaders and social reformers like Jotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B.R. Ambedkar and Periyar Ramaswami Naicker advocated and worked to:
options: Establish a society in which caste inequalities are absent
solution: Political leaders and social reformers like Jotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B.R. Ambedkar and Periyar Ramaswami Naicker advocated and worked to establish a society in which caste inequalities are absent.

stem: Which of the following factors has contributed to significant changes in the caste system in modern India?
options: Economic development, large-scale urbanisation, growth of literacy and education, occupational mobility, and the weakening of the position of landlords
solution: Economic development, large-scale urbanisation, growth of literacy and education, occupational mobility and the weakening of the position of landlords in villages have brought significant changes in the caste system.

stem: Despite constitutional prohibition, caste has not disappeared from India because:
options: Caste still influences life chances — some castes remain poor and discriminated against while others are advantaged
solution: Caste has not disappeared because it continues to be closely linked to economic status; caste and economic status are related, and casteism persists in the belief that caste is the sole basis of social community.

stem: 'Casteism' is rooted in the belief that:
options: Caste is the sole basis of social community, treating other castes as inferior, rival and enemy
solution: Casteism is rooted in the belief that caste is the sole basis of social community; members of one caste treat fellow caste members as their own and others as inferior, rival or enemy.

stem: When we speak of caste politics, one way it works is that each caste group tries to:
options: Become bigger by incorporating neighbouring castes or sub-castes that were earlier excluded, and enter into a coalition with other castes
solution: Each caste group tries to become bigger by incorporating within it neighbouring castes or sub-castes which were earlier excluded; various caste groups enter into a coalition with other castes and thus enter into a dialogue and negotiation.

stem: Which of the following statements about caste and politics is correct?
options: No party wins votes of only one caste
Elections are won purely on caste lines
Caste has no role in politics
The caste with the most votes always wins
solution: No parliamentary constituency has a clear majority of one single caste; hence every candidate and party needs to win the confidence of more than one caste to win elections — no party wins the votes of all voters of one caste.

stem: Politics too influences the caste system and caste identities by:
options: Bringing them into the political arena, making people more conscious of caste ties, and giving rise to caste-based movements and organisations
solution: Politics influences the caste system and caste identities by bringing them into the political arena — people become more conscious of their caste identities, and previously subordinate castes claim power, giving rise to demands for reservation and justice.

stem: The overlap of caste and economic differences produces the most disadvantaged groups. Which groups are largely poor, deprived and often face discrimination?
options: Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and sections of the backward castes
solution: Caste continues to be closely linked to economic status; a large proportion of low-caste people (the 'Scheduled Castes', 'Scheduled Tribes' and the backward castes) remain poor and face discrimination and exclusion.

stem: Focusing only on caste in politics can be harmful because it can:
options: Divert attention from other pressing issues like poverty, development and corruption, and can lead to tension, conflict and even violence
solution: If caste politics is over-emphasised, it can divert attention from issues of poverty, development and corruption, and can foster tensions, conflict and even violence.

stem: Which of the following is an example of the political expression of gender division that improved women's public role?
options: Women's movements demanding enhancement in the political and legal status of women and improving educational and career opportunities
solution: Political expression of gender divisions and political mobilisation helped improve women's role; agitation demanded enhancement of the political and legal status of women and improvement of their educational and career opportunities.

stem: In some countries such as Sweden, Norway and Finland, the participation of women in public life, especially in politics, is:
solution: In some parts of the world, notably Scandinavian countries like Sweden, Norway and Finland, the participation of women in public life, especially politics, is very high.

stem: The three kinds of social differences discussed in this chapter that can take the form of social divisions and expressions in politics are:
solution: The chapter deals with three kinds of social differences that can take the form of social divisions and inequalities — gender, religion and caste — and how they play out in politics.

stem: Which one of the following statements about the relationship between democracy and social diversity is correct?
options: Democracy must eliminate all social divisions
The expression of various kinds of social divisions in politics is not always dangerous and can be normal and healthy in a democracy
solution: In a democracy it is only natural that political parties would talk about these divisions, make different promises and address the deprivation of various communities; expression of social divisions in politics is quite normal and can be healthy.

stem: Which of the following would be considered communal politics?
options: Demand that all religions be treated equally
A political party seeking support by appealing to the religious sentiments and interests of one religious community in opposition to another
solution: Communal politics is based on the idea that religion is the principal basis of social community; when a party appeals to one religious group's interests against another's, that is communal politics.

stem: Gandhiji used to say that religion can never be separated from politics. What did he mean?
options: That the state should have an official religion
Not any particular religion (Hindu or Muslim), but moral values derived from all religions that should guide politics
That elections should be held in temples
solution: By religion, Gandhiji meant not any particular religion like Hinduism or Islam but moral values that inform all religions; he believed politics must be guided by ethics drawn from religion — very different from communal use of religion.

stem: Human rights groups in our country have argued that most of the victims of communal riots in our country are people from:
solution: Human rights groups have argued that most of the victims of communal riots in the country are people from religious minorities.

stem: The Constitution's approach to religion is best described as:
options: Secular — separating the state from religion, ensuring no state religion and equal treatment of all religions
solution: The Indian Constitution adopts a secular approach: there is no official religion, all citizens have freedom of religion, and the state does not discriminate on religious grounds but may intervene to ensure equality within communities.

stem: Occupational mobility and the loosening of the caste system in modern India are largely a result of:
options: Urbanisation, education, and constitutional and legal measures
solution: Large-scale urbanisation, growth of literacy and education, occupational mobility and constitutional-legal measures against caste discrimination have loosened the hold of the caste system.

stem: The sexual division of labour is a system in which:
options: Work is divided between men and women — women do household work while public activity is dominated by men
solution: The sexual division of labour is a system in which all work inside the home is either done by the women of the family or organised by them, while men are expected to do the paid work outside.

stem: Which of the following describes the current status of women in India politically?
options: Under-represented in Parliament and State Assemblies but with reservation and rising participation at the local level
solution: Women are still under-represented in Parliament and State Assemblies (touching around 14% in the Lok Sabha), but the one-third reservation in local bodies has brought over 10 lakh elected women representatives, boosting their participation.

stem: Which statement best captures the chapter's conclusion about social divisions in a democracy?
options: Every expression of social division threatens democracy
In a democracy, political expression of social divisions is normal; whether it divides or strengthens depends on how issues are raised and addressed
Social divisions should never be discussed in politics
solution: The expression of various kinds of social divisions in politics often results in their cancelling one another out and reducing their intensity; whether divisions strengthen or weaken democracy depends on how people perceive their identities and how leaders raise the issues.

stem: Reservation of seats and posts for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes is a constitutional measure aimed at:
options: Countering caste-based inequalities and giving disadvantaged communities access to education, jobs and political representation
solution: Constitutional reservations for SCs, STs and OBCs aim to counter historical caste-based inequalities by giving disadvantaged communities access to education, government jobs and political representation.

stem: Which of the following is TRUE about the relationship between caste and economic status?
options: There is a great deal of overlap between caste and economic inequality — the 'lower' castes are often poorer
The upper castes are always poor
Caste has no bearing on poverty
solution: There is a great deal of overlap between caste and economic inequality; the poor are concentrated among the low-caste groups, though the link is not absolute — some upper caste people are poor and some lower caste people are rich.

stem: The chapter argues that a positive way to deal with social diversity in a democracy is to:
options: Recognise and accommodate diversity through appropriate political and constitutional measures
solution: Democracies that recognise and accommodate social diversities through appropriate measures tend to be more stable and united than those that suppress differences.

stem: The declining child sex ratio is a matter of concern because it indicates:
options: Deep-rooted preference for sons and discrimination against girls, sometimes even before birth
solution: The declining child sex ratio indicates a deep-rooted preference for the male child and discrimination against girls, reflected in female foeticide, and is a serious social concern.

stem: Which one of these is an example of the state intervening in religion to promote equality, as allowed by the Constitution?
solution: The Constitution allows the state to intervene in religion to ensure equality — the abolition of untouchability (Article 17), which was practised in the name of religion, is a clear example.

stem: Which of the following pairs a reformer with the country/context correctly?
options: Periyar Ramaswami Naicker — anti-caste self-respect movement in India
solution: Periyar Ramaswami Naicker led the anti-caste Self-Respect Movement in India; along with Phule, Ambedkar and Gandhiji, he worked to establish a society without caste inequalities.

stem: The overall message of the chapter regarding gender, religion and caste in Indian politics is that:
options: These identities should be banned from politics
Democratic politics involves recognising these divisions and working towards equality, while communalism, sexism and casteism must be checked
Politics should ignore all social realities
solution: Democratic politics must recognise gender, religious and caste divisions and work towards equality and justice, while guarding against their negative forms — sexism, communalism and casteism — which harm democracy.

stem: The division of society based on the social expectations from men and women, rather than on biology, is called the:
solution: The gender division is based on social expectations and stereotypes rather than on biology; it is a form of hierarchical social division seen in most societies, but is often not recognised as division.

stem: The system in which women do most of the household work while men do the 'outside' paid work is called the:
solution: The sexual division of labour is a system in which all work inside the home is either done by the women of the family, or organised by them, while men are seen as the earners working outside.

stem: A person who believes in equal rights and opportunities for women and men is called a:
solution: A feminist is a woman or a man who believes in equal rights and opportunities for women and men; feminist movements have raised women's political and legal status.

stem: The child sex ratio in India (number of girl children per thousand boys) has been:
solution: The child sex ratio has been declining in India, falling to about 919 girls per 1,000 boys; this reflects the practice of sex-selective abortion (female foeticide) and preference for sons.

stem: To increase women's representation, one-third of the seats in local government bodies (panchayats and municipalities) are:
solution: One important measure to increase women's participation is that one-third of the seats in local government bodies — panchayats and municipalities — are now reserved for women.

stem: The proportion of women in the Lok Sabha has been quite low, at around:
solution: The percentage of elected women members in the Lok Sabha has remained low, touching only a little over 14 per cent of its total strength, far below their share in the population.

stem: Women's organisations have long demanded reservation of at least one-third of seats for women in:
options: The Lok Sabha and State Assemblies
solution: Women's organisations and activists have been demanding a similar reservation of at least one-third of seats in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, as exists in local bodies.

stem: Communalism, in its most common form, involves the belief that:
options: The followers of one religion form one community with common interests, superior to others
Religion has no role in society
solution: Communalism involves thinking of the followers of a religion as belonging to one community whose interests are the same and opposed to those of another; it can extend to the belief that one religion is superior to others.

stem: Which of the following is a provision of the Indian Constitution reflecting its secular character?
options: There is no official religion for the Indian state
solution: The Constitution provides that there is no official religion for the Indian state, gives every person freedom to profess, practise and propagate any religion, and prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion — reflecting secularism.

stem: The caste system, based on the hereditary occupational division sanctioned by rituals, is a social division largely peculiar to:
solution: Caste division is special to India; the caste system is an extreme form of the hereditary division of society, sanctioned by rituals, in which people are born into a caste that decides their occupation and status.

stem: Social reformers like Jotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B.R. Ambedkar and Periyar Ramaswami Naicker worked to:
options: Establish a society based on caste equality and end caste discrimination
solution: Political leaders and social reformers like Jotiba Phule, Gandhiji, B.R. Ambedkar and Periyar Ramaswami Naicker advocated and worked to establish a society in which caste inequalities are absent.

stem: Assertion (A): The child sex ratio in India is declining. Reason (R): Practices like sex-selective abortion reflect a preference for sons over daughters.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: A strong preference for sons has led families to use prenatal sex determination and abort female foetuses, causing the child sex ratio to fall — R explains A.

stem: Assertion (A): India is a secular state. Reason (R): The Constitution gives no religion the status of official religion and guarantees religious freedom to all.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: India is secular because the Constitution does not favour any religion as official and grants every citizen freedom of religion, along with equality regardless of religion — R explains A.

stem: Communal politics is based on the idea that:
options: Religion is the principal basis of social community and should determine political power
All religions should be respected equally
Religion has no place in society
solution: Communal politics is based on the belief that religion is the principal basis of social community, that people of one religion share common secular interests, and that one religious group can dominate others in the state.

stem: Which of the following would be considered an example of communal politics?
options: Using religious symbols and sentiment to mobilise voters of one religion
solution: Communal politics takes forms such as using religious appeals and symbols to gain political support, favouring one religious community, or a state acting to promote the domination of one religious group.

stem: Which of the following has contributed to changes in the caste system in modern India?
options: Urbanisation, education, occupational mobility and constitutional prohibition of discrimination
solution: Economic development, large-scale urbanisation, growth of literacy and education, occupational mobility, and the constitutional prohibition of caste discrimination have weakened the hold of the traditional caste hierarchy.

stem: When each caste tries to become bigger by incorporating neighbouring castes or sub-castes to gain political influence, it shows that:
options: Politics influences the caste system as much as caste influences politics
solution: Politics influences the caste system: castes that were earlier excluded from politics get political mobilisation, and various caste groups enter into coalitions, so caste and politics shape each other.

stem: The overlap of caste with economic inequality means that:
options: The 'lower' castes are often poorer and more disadvantaged
solution: When caste divisions overlap with economic inequalities, they produce the most disadvantaged groups; the castes that were regarded as low were also the poorest and remain socially and economically disadvantaged.

stem: Reservation of seats and posts for SCs, STs and OBCs is a way of:
options: Correcting historical injustices and giving disadvantaged groups a fair share
solution: Reservation in legislatures, jobs and education for the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes is a constitutional measure to correct historic caste discrimination and give the disadvantaged a fair share.

stem: Match the reformer with their focus: (i) Jotiba Phule (ii) B.R. Ambedkar (iii) Periyar Ramaswami Naicker — all worked against:
solution: Jotiba Phule, B.R. Ambedkar and Periyar Ramaswami Naicker all struggled against caste inequality and worked to build a society free of caste-based discrimination.

stem: Human rights groups have argued that most of the victims of communal riots in India are:
solution: Human rights groups have pointed out that most of the victims of communal riots in the country are people from the minority communities, highlighting the dangers of communal politics.

stem: The countries with high women's participation in public life, cited in the chapter, include:
solution: In some parts of the world, notably in the Scandinavian countries such as Sweden, Norway and Finland, the participation of women in public life and legislatures is very high.

stem: The Constitution's approach to religion (Indian secularism) is best described as:
options: Equal respect and protection to all religions, with no state religion
solution: Indian secularism gives equal respect and protection to all religions, does not adopt any state religion, guarantees religious freedom to all, and allows the state to intervene to ensure equality within religions.

stem: Which statement about the relationship between caste and politics is correct?
options: Caste influences politics and politics influences caste, but neither fully determines the other
Politics has no link with caste
solution: Caste and politics are related in both directions: parties consider caste while nominating candidates and forming governments, and political competition tends to change and weaken rigid caste identities — but no single caste can win elections alone.

stem: No single caste can win an election on its own because:
options: No parliamentary constituency has a clear majority of one caste, so parties need support across castes
solution: No parliamentary constituency in the country has a clear majority of one single caste; every candidate and party needs to win the confidence of more than one caste and community to succeed, limiting pure caste politics.

stem: The three social differences discussed in the chapter that can take a political form are:
solution: The chapter discusses three kinds of social differences — gender, religion and caste — and examines how each takes a political form and how democracy responds to them.

stem: The literacy rate among women in India, compared to men, is generally:
solution: According to the Census, the literacy rate among women is significantly lower than among men; on average, women have less access to education, which is one dimension of gender inequality.

stem: The 'sexual division of labour' does NOT mean that:
options: Women are incapable of doing outside work — it is a social arrangement, not natural
solution: The sexual division of labour is a socially assigned arrangement, not a natural one; women are perfectly capable of doing 'outside' work, but society tends to value men's work more and confine women to domestic roles.

stem: The positive way to deal with social diversity in a democracy, according to the chapter, is to:
options: Recognise and accommodate diversity through fair representation and equal rights
solution: The chapter argues that expressing and accommodating social divisions in politics is normal and can be healthy in a democracy, provided it is done through fair representation and equal rights, not domination.

stem: The 'patriarchal' system is one that values and gives more importance to:
options: Men and male authority over women
solution: Patriarchy refers to a system that values men more and gives them power over women; it is reflected in the sexual division of labour, unequal wages, preference for sons, and low representation of women in public life.

stem: The overall message of the chapter regarding gender, religion and caste is that:
options: Social divisions become dangerous when politics exploits them, but democracy can accommodate diversity fairly
Social divisions should never enter politics
solution: The chapter concludes that gender, religion and caste can become sources of conflict when politics exploits them (as in communalism or casteism), but with fair accommodation and equal rights, democracy can handle diversity constructively.

stem: The women's movement demanding equal rights and opposing patriarchy is part of the political expression of:
solution: The political expression of gender division, and the political mobilisation of women, has helped improve women's role in public life; feminist movements demand equality and challenge patriarchy.

stem: An example of the state intervening in religion to ensure equality is:
solution: Indian secularism permits state intervention in religion to promote equality; the abolition of untouchability by the Constitution, despite its religious sanction, is a key example of such intervention.

stem: Occupational mobility and the loosening of the caste system in modern India occurred mainly due to:
solution: With urbanisation, growth of industries, spread of education and new occupations, the link between caste and occupation weakened, loosening the rigid traditional caste system, especially in cities.

stem: Which of the following describes the current status of women in India?
options: Progress has been made, but inequality persists in wages, education, safety and representation
Women have more rights than men
solution: While women's political and legal status has improved, women in India still face inequality — lower literacy and wages, discrimination, and low representation in legislatures — showing gender inequality persists.

stem: The main reason a purely caste-based or religion-based politics is considered undesirable is that it:
options: Can divide society, cause conflict, and neglect real issues of development and welfare
solution: Politics based solely on caste or religion can deepen social divisions, breed tension and violence, and divert attention from crucial issues like development, poverty and welfare, which is why it is seen as harmful.

stem: The expression of caste in politics is NOT entirely negative because it can:
options: Give voice and representation to hitherto oppressed and disadvantaged caste groups
solution: Caste politics can help disadvantaged and previously oppressed communities gain political mobilisation, demand representation and access to power, which has strengthened democracy by including marginalised groups.

stem: The demand for reserving one-third of seats for women in Parliament and assemblies is meant to address:
options: The very low representation of women in these bodies
The excess of women in politics
solution: Since women's share in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies is very low, women's organisations demand reservation of one-third of the seats to ensure adequate representation of women in the higher legislatures.

stem: Secularism as a state ideal is important in a diverse society like India because it:
options: Prevents any one religion from dominating the state and protects the freedom of all
solution: Secularism ensures that the state does not favour any religion, protects the religious freedom and equality of all citizens, and guards against communal domination, which is vital in a religiously diverse country.

stem: The example of unequal wages for women doing the same work as men illustrates:
options: Economic gender inequality in the workplace
solution: Although the Equal Remuneration Act requires equal pay, in many areas women are still paid less than men for the same work, illustrating persistent economic inequality based on gender.

stem: The term 'patriarchy' refers to a system that values:
options: Men more and gives men more power, dominating over women in society
solution: Patriarchy literally means rule by father; it is a system that values men more and gives them power to dominate women. Our society is still male-dominated and women face disadvantage, discrimination and oppression in various ways.
